_comment: Per-designator corrections applied to fab/CPL_JLCPCB.csv after `kicad-cli pcb export pos` has written it (scripts/61_make_bom_cpl.py). A CPL rotation is not a property of the board: it is the angle between the board's footprint and the orientation the assembler's own library holds the part in. When the two libraries disagree, the board must not be turned to match -- the copper is right -- so the number is corrected here, on the one file that talks to the assembler, and the reason is written down next to it. Keys are designators; keys beginning with _ are notes. Every entry needs a why.

U_MCU.why: ESP32-WROOM-32UE-N4, LCSC C701344. JLC's / EasyEDA's footprint for this part is drawn with the module's long axis along Y, which is +90 degrees CCW from the footprint on this board (all 38 pads map onto ours after a +90 rotation, and both footprints take the centre of the pad bounding box as their origin, so Mid X and Mid Y are unchanged). The board's own orientation stays 0: nothing on the PCB moves, only the number JLC's placement machine is told. Recorded with the part swap in data/bom_fixes_2026-08-28.json (lead, 2026-08-28). What to check on JLC's Confirm Parts Placement screen: the module's pad-free end (the end the 32E carried its antenna on) points west, towards U_ADS.
